questions.question: A shopkeeper sold two articles for ₹560 each. He incurred no loss and made no profit in the transaction because one article was sold at a loss of 16(2)/(3)% and the other article was sold at a profit of:
questions.solution:
Given:

Selling price of each article = ₹560

Loss incurred on selling one article = 16(2)/(3)% = 50/3 %

Concept used:

Selling Price = Cost Price - Cost Price × Loss%

Selling Price = Cost Price + Cost Price × Gain%

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the article that is sold at loss be Q.

According to the question,

Q - Q × 50/3 % = 560

⇒ Q - Q/6 = 560

⇒ 5Q/6 = 560

⇒ Q/6 = 112

⇒ Q = 112 × 6

⇒ Q = 672

Let the cost price of the other article be R that is sold is G% profit.

According to the question,

R + 672 = 560 × 2

⇒ R = 1120 - 672

⇒ R = 448

The cost price of the other article = ₹448

According to the question,

448 + 448 × G% = 560

⇒ 448 (1 + G/100) = 560

⇒ (1 + G/100) = 560/448

⇒ (1 + G/100) = 1.25

⇒ G/100 = 1.25 - 1

⇒ G/100 = 0.25

⇒ G = 25

**∴ The other article was sold at a profit of 25%.**

questions.question: If a number N is divisible by 3, then which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
Given:

N is divisible by 3

Calculation:

Considering the given options as follows:

Option 1)

N is divisible by 3 doesn't necessarily mean N is also divisible by 6.

For example, 21 is divisible by 3 but 21 isn't divisible by 6. Similarly, (21 + 6) i.e., 27 isn't divisible by 6 either.

So, we can't conclude that (N + 6) is divisible by 6.

Option 2)

2 isn't divisible by 3.

So even though N is divisible by 3, (N + 2) isn't divisible by 3.

Option 3)

Let's suppose N = 9.

9 is divisible by 3 but 9² is not divisible by 6.

So if N2 is not divisible by 6 for N = 9, we can't conclude that N2 is divisible by 6.

Option 4)

12 is divisible by 3.

N is divisible by 3.

So, (N + 12) must be divisible by 3.

**∴ (N + 12) is divisible by 3.**

questions.question: The length (in m) of the longest pole that can be fitted in a room of dimensions 24 m × 12 m × 3 m is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Dimensions of the room = 24 m × 12 m × 3 m

Concept used:

Length of the longest diagonal of a cuboid = sqrt {L² + B² + H²}

where L, B, and H are the length, breadth, and height respectively. 

Calculation:

The aforementioned room is in a form of a cuboid.

So, the length of the longest pole that can be fitted in the room is equal to the length of the longest diagonal of the cuboid.

According to the concept,

The length of the longest pole that can be fitted in the room

⇒ sqrt {24² + 12² + 3²}

⇒ sqrt {729}

⇒ 27 m

**∴ The length of the longest pole that can be fitted in a room of dimensions 24 m × 12 m × 3 m is 27m.**

questions.question: If x² + y² + z² + 26 = 2(4x + y + 3z), then find the value of x + y + z.
questions.solution:
Given:

x2 + y2 + z2 + 26 = 2(4x + y + 3z)

Concept used:

(A - B)² = A² - 2AB + B²

If A² + B² + C² = 0 then A = B = C = 0 i.e., A + B + C = 0

Calculation:

x2 + y2 + z2 + 26 = 2(4x + y + 3z)

⇒ x2 + y2 + z2 + 26 = 8x + 2y + 6z

⇒ (x2 - 8x + 16) + (y2 - 2y + 1) + (z2 - 6z + 9) = 0

⇒ (x - 4)² + (y - 1)² + (z - 3)² = 0

According to the concept,

Now, (x - 4) + (y - 1) + (z - 3) = 0

⇒ x + y + z = 4 + 1 + 3

⇒ x + y + z = 8

**∴ The value of x + y + z is 8.**

questions.question: The average weight of some children in a group was 42 kg. When 5 children of average weight 48 kg join the group or 5 children of average weight 37 kg leave the group, the average weight of children in both cases remains equal. How many children were there in the group initially?
questions.solution:
Given:

The average weight of some children in a group was 42 kg. 

When 5 children of average weight 48 kg join the group or 5 children of average weight 37 kg leave the group, the average weight of children in both cases remains equal.

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

Let there be N number of students initially.

The average weight of the group when 5 children with an average weight of 48 kg join the group

⇒ (42 × N + 5 × 48)/(N + 5)

The average weight of the group when 5 children with average weight of 37 kg leave the group

⇒ (42 × N - 5 × 37)/(N - 5)

According to the question,

(42 × N + 5 × 48)/(N + 5) = (42 × N - 5 × 37)/(N - 5)

⇒ (42N + 240)/(N + 5) = (42N - 185)/(N - 5)

⇒ (N + 5)/(N - 5) = (42N + 240)/(42N - 185)

Using componendo-dividendo method

⇒ (N + 5 + N - 5)/(N + 5 - N + 5) = (42N + 240 + 42N - 185)/(42N + 240 - 42N + 185)

⇒ 2N/10 = (84N + 55)/425

⇒ N/5 = (84N + 55)/425

⇒ 425N = 420N + 275

⇒ 425N - 420N = 275

⇒ N = 275/5

⇒ N = 55

∴ There were 55 children initially.

questions.question: The ratio of the number of animals in zoo A to the number of animals in zoo B is 6 ∶ 5. If zoo B has 65 animals in the beginning, how many animals must be transferred from zoo A to B so that the ratio of animals in zoo A and zoo B becomes 6 ∶ 7?
questions.solution:
Given:

The ratio of the number of animals in zoo A to the number of animals in zoo B is 6 ∶ 5.

Calculation:

Let the number of animals at Zoo A and B be 6Q and 5Q respectively.

According to the question,

5Q = 65

⇒ Q = 13

So, the number of animals at Zoo B

⇒ 6 × 13 = 78

Let R animals must be transferred from zoo A to B.

According to the question,

(78 - R)/(65 + R) = 6/7

⇒ (78 - R) × 7 = (65 + R) × 6

⇒ 546 - 7R = 390 + 6R

⇒ 7R + 6R = 546 - 390

⇒ 13R = 156

⇒ R = 156/13

⇒ R = 12

**∴ 12 animals must be transferred from zoo A to B so that the ratio of animals in zoo A and zoo B becomes 6 ∶ 7.**

questions.question: A and B can do a certain work in 25 and 20 days, respectively. They work together for 4 days. The remaining work is completed by C in 8 days. C alone can complete 40% of the original work in:
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B can do a certain work in 25 and 20 days, respectively. They work together for 4 days.

The remaining work is completed by C in 8 days.

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency (Work done per day) × Total time taken 

Calculation:

LCM (25, 20, 8) = 200

Let the total work be the LCM of the time taken by different workers.

So, total work = 200 units

The efficiency of A = 200/25 = 8 units

The efficiency of B = 200/20 = 10 units

Work done by A & B together in 4 days

⇒ (8 + 10) × 4

⇒ 72 units

Remaining work = (200 - 72) = 128 units

The efficiency of C = 128/8 = 16 units

Now, C alone can complete 40% of the original work in

⇒ (200/16) × 40%

⇒ 12.5 × 40%

⇒ 5 days

**∴ C alone can complete 40% of the original work in 5 days.**

questions.question: A 200 m long train crosses a pole in 10 seconds. Another train of length 250 m crosses a platform which is 200 m long in 15 seconds. If both trains move in opposite directions, how much time (in seconds) will they take to cross each other completely?
questions.solution:
Given:

A 200 m long train crosses a pole in 10 seconds.

Another train of length 250 m crosses a platform which is 200 m long in 15 seconds.

Concept used:

While a train crosses a platform, it crosses the sum of its length and the length of the platform

While a train crosses a pole, it crosses its own length.

When a train completely crosses another train, it basically crosses the sum of the lengths of the two trains.

Relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds while two bodies are coming from the opposite direction.

Time × Speed = Distance

Calculation:

Speed of the first train

⇒ 200/10 = 20 m/s

Speed of the second train

⇒ {(250 + 200) over 15} = 30 m/s

Relative speed while approaching each other from the opposite direction

⇒ (20 + 30) = 50 m/s

Time taken by the trains to cross each other completely

⇒ {200 + 250} over 50

⇒ 9 seconds

**∴ If both trains move in opposite directions, they will take 9 seconds to cross each other completely.**
